articleSummary: Việt Nam reports a sharp rise in invasive meningococcal disease caused by Neisseria meningitidis, with 95 cases in the past year vs 21 the year before and 3 deaths. articleHeadline: Invisible danger in traditional dishes alarms health authorities
articleSummary: Five severe botulinum toxin poisoning cases in Da Nang linked to fermented fish highlight ongoing risk in Vietnam. Early administration within 48–72 hours can shorten ventilation and aid recovery; delays worsen outcomes. Prevention stressed: avoid damaged packaging, thoroughly boil/steam canned foods for at least 10 minutes and seek urgent care for symptoms such as ptosis, dysphagia, and weakness.

articleHeadline: World Tuberculosis Day 2026: What is drug-resistant tuberculosis and how it's diagnosed
articleSummary: World Tuberculosis Day 2026 highlights drug-resistant TB (DR-TB), where Mycobacterium tuberculosis no longer responds to standard anti-TB drugs, complicating treatment and increasing transmission. WHO regards DR-TB as a major societal issue; early diagnosis and proper medication are essential. Diagnosis confirms TB infection and tests for drug resistance, using Ziehl-Neelsen or fluorescence microscopy to detect TB but not resistance. Drug susceptibility testing can be phenotypic (culture-based) or genotypic (mutations indicating resistance). Line probe assays (LPA) and whole-genome sequencing (WGS) rapidly detect resistance across drugs, with LPA results in 1–2 days. articleSummary: Tuberculosis (TB) in India remains a major public health challenge, with over 26 lakh cases recorded in 2025 and more than 300,000 deaths annually. articleSummary: Chikungunya outbreak in Dourados, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil prompts community donations. The Associação Comercial e Empresarial de Dourados (ACED) joined the Emergency Support Committee for the Indigenous Reserve and serves as a donation drop-off site at 1480 Av. Joaquim Teixeira Alves, Centro (Mon–Fri, 7:30–17:30). Other drop-offs at Câmara Municipal de Dourados and OAB Dourados/Itaporã. The committee aims to organize emergency collection, logistics, and communication to aid families facing food and hydration shortages. Epidemiological bulletin reports a 42% increase in cases under investigation in two days, totaling 572 suspected and 274 confirmed as of 19/03, with >150 hospitalizations and 4 deaths (three elderly aged 60, 69, 73 and a 3‑month‑old infant).

articleSummary: One in five tuberculosis infections go undetected or unreported, per WHO Europe. In 2024 Europe officially logged about 162,000 TB cases, with an estimated true burden around 204,000. Diagnostic delays amplify transmission and hinder care, undermining early-detection and treatment goals. Globally, TB remains the deadliest infectious disease, with roughly 11 million infections and over 1.2 million deaths in 2024, concentrated in low-resource settings; India, Indonesia, China, Pakistan, and the Philippines are among the hardest hit. World TB Day is March 24; TB is airborne and commonly presents with persistent cough, chest pain, weight loss, night sweats, and fever. articleSummary: World TB Day on 24 March commemorates Robert Koch’s 1882 discovery of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the lung-focused cause of tuberculosis. Country shares: India 25%, Indonesia 10%, the Philippines 6.8%, China 6.5%, Pakistan 6.3%, Nigeria 4.8%, DR Congo 3.9%, Bangladesh 3.6%. Of cases, 54% were adult men, 35% adult women, 11% children. articleSummary: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) uses a lipid-rich outer membrane to switch between active and dormant states, aiding immune evasion and antibiotic tolerance. articleHeadline: Genital TB And The Mystery Of Chronic Pelvic Pain | World Tuberculosis Day 2026
articleSummary: Genital tuberculosis is an extrapulmonary TB form affecting the female reproductive tract, presenting with chronic pelvic pain rather than cough or fever. In India, where TB is common, genital TB may go unrecognized as doctors attribute symptoms to endometriosis, pelvic inflammatory disease, or hormonal imbalance. On World Tuberculosis Day 2026, pulmonologists highlight that TB can operate outside the lungs and manifest with nonspecific symptoms; Genital TB causes pelvic pain and other subtle signs that pattern-recognition alone may miss. Dr. Arup Halder of CK Birla Hospitals/ CMRI emphasizes that absence of classic TB signals often delays diagnosis. The article stresses the need to consider extrapulmonary TB in persistent pelvic pain cases, to avoid misdiagnosis and ensure appropriate testing and treatment.
